messages.author: dc8b4131b39a099f
messages.subject: offset argument and parboot
parts:
Dear unmarked users-

I am using an offset(log(sampling_area)) argument in pcount model
statements. I'm wondering if this could influence the results of
parametric bootstrapping to assess model GOF. I'm consistently
getting very large mean differences between t0 and t_B, regardless of
species and model parameters. Thanks for your input. Best,

Matt

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] offset argument and parboot
parts:
Hi Matt,

I just double checked the code and parboot does acknowledge offsets, so I don't think there is a problem. This little simulation doesn't suggest a problem either. Are there any unusual features of the data, eg outliers?



set.seed(1032)
R <- 100
J <- 10
x1 <- rnorm(R)
x2 <- runif(R, 0.5, 1)
lam <- exp(0 + -1*x1) * x2
N <- rpois(R, lam)
table(N)
y <- matrix(NA, R, J)
for(i in 1:R) {
    y[i,] <- rbinom(J, N[i], 0.5)
}

library(unmarked)
umf <- unmarkedFramePCount(y=y, siteCovs=data.frame(x1=x1, x2=x2))
summary(umf)

(m1 <- pcount(~1 ~x1 + offset(log(x2)), umf, K=50))
pb1 <- parboot(m1, nsim=100, report=5)

> pb1

Call: parboot(object = m1, nsim = 100, report = 5)

Parametric Bootstrap Statistics:
     t0 mean(t0 - t_B) StdDev(t0 - t_B) Pr(t_B > t0)
SSE 586             48             85.8        0.257

t_B quantiles:
     0% 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% 100%
SSE 349  408 479 526 587   757  785

t0 = Original statistic compuated from data
t_B = Vector of bootstrap samples




Richard

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] offset argument and parboot
parts:
hi Matt,
 The other explanation is that none of your models fit the data right?  Kind of a bummer, but also not out of the ordinary. 
 You could also try using log(AREA) is a covariate (with effect estimated).  It might be reasonable to expect that E[N] does not scale with area (e.g., diminishing returns, competition, etc..)
regards
andy
